_readme: The plain-English layer. `content/` stays the auditable extraction from the trainers' PDFs; this file is
what we add on the way to the learner so a first-week reader is never stuck. Three jobs, one file:
acronyms      — spelled out the first time each level mentions them, in words not more letters.
substitutions — hard formal words replaced by the everyday one, in prose only (never in code).
glossary      — the words that stay, because they ARE the subject, explained in one short line and
shown under the level the learner is reading.
Rules a gate checks (pnpm content:lint): an entry's `plain` is at most 20 words, uses no word from
`substitutions`, and does not hide another acronym inside it. Add a term with one line, not a paragraph.

acronyms.HTML: the markup that names what is on a page
acronyms.CSS: the rules that say how the page looks
acronyms.JSON: plain text that holds data in names and values
acronyms.URL: the web address you type or paste
acronyms.HTTP: the way a browser and a server talk to each other

acronyms.DNS: the book that turns a name into a number

acronyms.IP: the number that identifies one machine on a network
acronyms.RAM: fast, temporary memory that forgets when power goes off
acronyms.CPU: the chip that runs your instructions, one at a time
acronyms.GPU: a chip built to do many sums at once, for pictures
acronyms.SSD: storage with no moving parts, so it is fast and tough
acronyms.HDD: storage on a spinning disk — cheap, slow, fragile
acronyms.BIOS: the first program a PC runs, before Windows starts
acronyms.UEFI: the newer BIOS, with a mouse and a file browser
acronyms.DOM: the page as a tree the code can reach into
acronyms.API: a door one program uses to ask another for help
acronyms.MFA: a second proof it is you, usually a code on your phone
acronyms.VPN: a private tunnel for your traffic across a public network
acronyms.WAN: a network that joins places far apart
acronyms.VLAN: one cable split into several separate networks
acronyms.ISP: the company that gives you the internet
acronyms.NAT: how one public address serves a whole building
acronyms.SMTP: how mail leaves your server on its way out
acronyms.IMAP: how mail is read from the server, kept in sync
acronyms.KPI: the one number that tells you if it is working
acronyms.SEO: the work that makes a page easier to find in search
acronyms.CTR: how many people click, out of how many see it
acronyms.CPC: what you pay each time someone clicks your ad
acronyms.ROI: what you made back, against what you spent
acronyms.CRM: the book of every customer and what you promised them
acronyms.CMS: a tool to change a site without touching code
acronyms.PNG: a sharp image that can hold clear edges and transparency
acronyms.JPEG: a photo format that shrinks by dropping detail
acronyms.SVG: a picture drawn from shapes, so it stays sharp at any size
acronyms.RGB: colour made from red, green and blue light
acronyms.CMYK: colour mixed from four inks, for printing
acronyms.UI: the parts of a product you touch and see
acronyms.UX: how the whole task feels to the person doing it
acronyms.OS: the program that runs the machine and its apps
acronyms.CPU-usage: how busy the chip is, as a share of what it can do
acronyms.CSV: a table saved as plain text, one line per row
acronyms.PDF: a fixed page, made to be read or printed, not edited
acronyms.USB: the plug nearly every small device uses
acronyms.QR: the square code a phone camera reads
acronyms.WI-FI: networking over radio instead of cable
acronyms.FAQ: the answers page for questions people keep asking
acronyms.BVN: your Bank Verification Number that links your Nigerian bank accounts
acronyms.OTP: a one-time secret code sent to your phone to confirm an action
acronyms.POS: the card machine used in shops and by cash agents
acronyms.USSD: short star-and-hash phone codes like *901# that work without data
acronyms.SIM: the small chip inside your phone that holds your phone number
acronyms.PIN: your secret four- or six-digit number — never share it
acronyms.ATM: the cash machine outside a bank
acronyms.2FA: two-step sign-in using your password plus a code on your phone
acronyms.SQL: the language used to ask a database for information
acronyms.CLI: a text window where you type commands instead of clicking buttons
acronyms.IDE: the main app where programmers write and test code
acronyms.SSL: the security lock that scrambles data between a browser and a website
acronyms.TLS: the modern security lock that keeps website connections private
acronyms.SSH: a secure way to control another computer using typed commands
acronyms.FTP: an older way to copy files to or from a remote computer
acronyms.CDN: nearby servers around the world that deliver website files faster
acronyms.SDK: a starter kit of tools for building apps on a platform
acronyms.CTA: the button or link telling a visitor what to do next
acronyms.B2C: businesses selling straight to everyday customers
acronyms.CAC: Nigeria's Corporate Affairs Commission where businesses are registered
acronyms.TIN: Tax Identification Number for a person or business
acronyms.VAT: Value Added Tax added to goods and services
acronyms.GIF: an image format often used for short looping clips
acronyms.MP4: the standard file format for video that plays on any phone or PC
acronyms.MP3: the standard compressed file format for audio and music
acronyms.FPS: frames per second — how many still pictures play each second in video
acronyms.DPI: dots per inch — how sharp a printed image will look on paper
acronyms.HEX: a six-character colour code starting with #, like #1a365d
acronyms.SSID: the name of a wireless network you pick on your phone or laptop
acronyms.MAC: the unique hardware address built into a network card
acronyms.GUI: screens with buttons, icons and menus you click with a mouse or finger
acronyms.CRUD: the four basic data actions: create, read, update and delete
acronyms.JWT: a signed digital pass that proves you are signed in
acronyms.CORS: browser rules controlling which websites may ask your server for data
acronyms.SPA: a web app that updates one page smoothly instead of reloading
acronyms.PWA: a website you can save to your phone home screen like an app

typing-computer-basics.tagline: Never used a computer comfortably before? Start right here — mouse, keyboard, files, folders and confident typing from zero.
typing-computer-basics.summary: This is the friendliest starting point in the academy. You learn what every part of a computer does, how to type without hunting for keys, how to save and find files neatly, and how to browse safely.

microsoft-office.tagline: Create clean letters in Word, smart budgets in Excel and clear slide decks in PowerPoint that any employer will respect.
microsoft-office.summary: Almost every office job asks for Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Step by step, you will write formatted documents, run real formulas and charts, and build presentations from scratch.

data-entry.tagline: Turn messy paper records and forms into clean, accurate spreadsheets fast — with zero formula headaches.
data-entry.summary: Businesses, hospitals, schools and NGOs need people who can enter, clean and check data without mistakes. You will master fast keyboard habits, sorting, filtering and error-checking.

digital-productivity.tagline: Work smoothly with professional email, Google Docs, cloud folders, online calendars and team tools from phone or laptop.
digital-productivity.summary: Modern remote and office work happens in the cloud. Learn how to write sharp emails, share files safely without losing versions, organise meetings and keep your work tidy.

graphic-design.tagline: Design eye-catching flyers, church & event posters, social media graphics and brand logos that clients happily pay for.
graphic-design.summary: You do not need to know how to draw to become a strong designer. Learn colour, layout, clear fonts and practical design tools so every poster or flyer looks clean and professional.

photography.tagline: Take sharp, well-lit portraits, event photos and product shots — using either a camera or the phone in your pocket.
photography.summary: Good photos come from light, framing and timing, not just expensive gear. Learn how to control exposure, pose people naturally, shoot products and edit clean final images.

video-editing.tagline: Cut raw clips into smooth, engaging videos with clean sound, captions and pacing for YouTube, TikTok, Reels and clients.
video-editing.summary: Every brand and creator needs an editor who can turn rough footage into a story people watch to the end. Learn cutting, audio cleanup, titles, transitions and exporting.

content-creation.tagline: Plan, script, shoot and publish helpful videos and posts on your phone that grow an audience and bring in customers.
content-creation.summary: Stop guessing what to post. Learn how to pick a clear topic, write strong hooks, film with good lighting and audio on a phone, and turn views into real income.

social-media-management.tagline: Run business pages professionally — content calendars, captions, customer replies and clear monthly results reports.
social-media-management.summary: Small businesses want someone reliable to handle their Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and WhatsApp presence. Learn how to plan a month of posts, grow engagement and charge monthly retainers.

digital-marketing.tagline: Bring real paying customers to any business using search, WhatsApp funnels, landing pages and smart online ads.
digital-marketing.summary: Learn how people discover and buy things online in plain steps: choosing the right audience, writing offers that make sense, running small ad tests safely and tracking what worked.

web-design.tagline: Build clean, mobile-friendly websites for businesses, portfolios and shops — laid out clearly for phones and laptops.
web-design.summary: Every business needs a trustworthy home online. Learn how web pages are structured, styled and arranged so visitors immediately understand what is offered and how to get in touch.

web-development.tagline: Make websites interactive with real JavaScript — buttons, forms, live updates and practical web apps from zero.
web-development.summary: Go beyond static pages and learn how code actually thinks. Every concept — variables, functions, page updates and saving data — is explained in everyday English before you type a single line.

cybersecurity.tagline: Protect phones, bank apps, company accounts and networks from scams, hackers, phishing links and data loss.
cybersecurity.summary: With bank apps, POS machines and WhatsApp scams everywhere, security is an essential skill. Learn how attacks happen in real life and the exact habits and tools that stop them.

computer-repairs.tagline: Diagnose, fix, upgrade and service laptops and desktop PCs safely — from slow Windows systems to hardware faults.
computer-repairs.summary: Broken and slow computers are everywhere, and skilled technicians stay busy. Learn what every internal part does, how to troubleshoot step by step without guessing, and how to price repairs fairly.

online-teaching.tagline: Turn any skill or school subject you know into clear, engaging online classes that students finish and recommend.
online-teaching.summary: Teaching online is very different from talking in a room. Learn how to break lessons into simple steps, keep learners active on Zoom or WhatsApp, grade fairly and run your own paid cohorts.

business-freelancing.tagline: Turn your practical skill into steady income — find clients, price your work confidently, send invoices and get paid.
business-freelancing.summary: Having a skill is half the job; getting paid fairly for it is the other half. Learn how to package your service, talk to clients, avoid unpaid extra work and manage your business money.
